name: Remotion
summary: Teaches the agent to build videos as React components: compositions, sequences, useCurrentFrame(), interpolate() and spring(). Reference files cover Three.js/React Three Fiber scenes and Lottie embedding.
when: Programmatic, data-driven or templated video: product explainers, social clips, animated charts, captions.
prompt: Use the remotion skill. Create a 10-second 1080x1080 composition that animates our three Q3 metrics in with spring() and renders to out/q3.mp4.
steps: Agent loads SKILL.md and its rule files (timing, sequencing, assets).
Scaffolds a Remotion project and writes a Composition in src/.
Previews in Remotion Studio (npx remotion studio).
Renders with npx remotion render to an MP4 artifact.
run: cd remotion-video && npx remotion render SkillsIntro out/skills-intro.mp4

name: GSAP Web Animation
summary: Part of a web-motion pack covering GSAP timelines, ScrollTrigger, SplitText, SVG, Lottie, micro-interactions, page transitions and 60fps performance rules.
when: Scroll-driven storytelling, landing-page hero sequences, orchestrated UI choreography.
prompt: Use the gsap-web skill. Build a hero where the headline splits into characters and staggers in, then pin the section and scrub a 3-step timeline on scroll.
steps: Agent reads the skill's GSAP rules (timeline-first, transforms only, cleanup on unmount).
Writes a gsap.timeline() with labelled steps and ScrollTrigger config.
Respects prefers-reduced-motion with gsap.matchMedia().
Ships an HTML/JS artifact you open in a browser.

outputs.caption: Pipeline hero: SplitText + DrawSVG on one master timeline, ?t=N seek harness, tiered reduced motion

run: open outputs/gsap-web/pipeline-hero.html   # add ?t=2 to freeze a frame

name: SVG Animation
summary: Stroke draw-on, path morphing and motion along a path, choosing between CSS, SMIL and GSAP for each job, with a seekable harness and a reduced-motion static end state.
when: Line-art reveals, route maps, logo draw-ons, icons that move along a path.
prompt: Use the svg-animation skill. Draw a route through three stops with stroke draw-on and a dot that rides the path, CSS only.
steps: Agent picks the lightest driver (CSS here: pathLength=1 + dashoffset).
Uses offset-path for the rider so it follows the same curve.
Adds a ?t=N seek harness and screenshots start, middle and end.
Gates the motion behind prefers-reduced-motion and shows the final state instead.

outputs.caption: Route through Database → Artifact → Execution: stroke draw-on + offset-path rider, CSS only

name: Lottie
output: Vector animation JSON embedded in a page or video
source: iart-ai/web-animation-skills (lottie skill) and Remotion Lottie rules
summary: Guides the agent through loading, controlling and segment-playing After Effects Lottie files, plus wiring them to hover, scroll or state changes.
when: Designer-made icon animations, onboarding illustrations, loaders exported from After Effects.
prompt: Use the lottie skill. Embed success.json, play frames 0-60 on submit and loop 60-90 while the request is pending.
steps: Agent identifies the Lottie asset and its markers/segments.
Writes lottie.loadAnimation() with renderer, loop and autoplay set.
Binds playSegments() to UI events.
Produces an HTML artifact or a Remotion <Lottie> layer.
code:
const anim = lottie.loadAnimation({container: el, path: 'success.json', autoplay: false});
form.onsubmit = () => anim.playSegments([0, 60], true);

outputs.caption: Hand-authored Lottie JSON (trim-path ring + check, pop, halo) played with lottie-web

name: HyperFrames
runtime: HTML + GSAP (adapters: Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS, WAAPI, TypeGPU)
install: npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes -s hyperframes -s hyperframes-cli
summary: Video as HTML: CSS controls the look, a GSAP timeline controls time, and the HyperFrames renderer captures it frame by frame into a video. Seven runtime adapters let one scene mix GSAP, Lottie, Three.js and more.
when: Agent-authored marketing videos and title sequences when you'd rather write HTML than React.
prompt: Use the hyperframes skill. Make a 6s 16:9 title card: logo draws on, tagline types in, then everything wipes to black. Render to title.mp4.
steps: Agent reads the hyperframes skill first (it routes to sub-skills).
Writes an HTML composition with data-* timing attributes and a paused GSAP timeline.
Previews in the browser, scrubbing the timeline.
Renders with the HyperFrames CLI into an MP4 artifact.
code: Ship faster

outputs.caption: 6s 1920×1080 title card, passes `hyperframes check`, rendered by the HyperFrames CLI

name: GSAP in Remotion
summary: Bridges GSAP into Remotion compositions by seeking a paused timeline to the current frame, so you get GSAP easing, morphing and text effects beyond interpolate() and spring().
when: You already use Remotion but need GSAP-level easing, MorphSVG or SplitText in video.
prompt: Use the gsap-animation skill. In my Remotion composition, drive a paused GSAP timeline from useCurrentFrame() to morph the logo outline into a circle.
steps: Agent builds a paused gsap.timeline() in a ref.
On each frame, seeks tl.seek(frame / fps).
Keeps rendering deterministic (no requestAnimationFrame).
Renders through Remotion to MP4.

outputs.caption: GsapTitle: SplitText chars + DrawSVG ring, paused GSAP timeline seeked to frame / fps

run: cd remotion-video && npx remotion render GsapTitle out/gsap-title.mp4

name: Manim
install: pip install manim   # skill: NousResearch hermes-agent manim-video
summary: 3Blue1Brown-style mathematical and algorithm animations: Scenes, MathTex, Transform, and camera moves, rendered with the manim CLI.
when: Equations, proofs, geometry, algorithm walk-throughs and teaching videos.
prompt: Use the manim skill. Animate the Pythagorean theorem: draw a right triangle, grow squares on each side, then transform a²+b² into c².
steps: Agent writes a Python file with a Scene subclass and construct().
Uses self.play(Create(...), Transform(...)) for each beat.
Runs manim -pqh scene.py PythagorasScene.
Collects the MP4 from media/videos as the artifact.
note: Scene written (outputs/manim/pythagoras.py) but not rendered: Manim needs system cairo/pango headers (sudo) that the build machine lacks. See outputs/manim/STATUS.md.

name: Anime.js
summary: Lightweight JS animation: staggered grids, SVG line drawing, path following and timelines with a small footprint.
when: Small pages where GSAP is overkill; SVG stroke drawing; grid stagger effects.
prompt: Use the animejs skill. Make a 10x10 dot grid that ripples out from wherever I click using stagger({grid, from}).
steps: Agent creates the DOM/SVG targets.
Writes animate()/timeline calls with stagger and easing.
Adds reduced-motion fallback.
Ships a single HTML artifact.

outputs.caption: SVG line drawing + 13×13 grid stagger from center; click a dot to ripple from it

name: Three.js / WebGL
summary: 3D motion: scene/camera/renderer setup, animation loops, GLTF animation mixers, shader uniforms over time and performance budgets.
when: 3D product spins, particle hero sections, shader backgrounds.
prompt: Use the threejs skill. Build a full-screen particle field that slowly orbits and reacts to the mouse, capped at 60fps on mobile.
steps: Agent sets up renderer, camera and scene.
Writes the setAnimationLoop() update with delta time.
Adds resize handling and devicePixelRatio caps.
Delivers an HTML artifact (or an R3F component).

outputs.caption: 12,000 seeded particles on a torus knot, pure frame(t) render, mouse parallax

name: CSS & Web Animations API
runtime: CSS keyframes, transitions, WAAPI, View Transitions
summary: Dependency-free motion. The frontend-design skill's rule: one orchestrated moment beats scattered effects, motion should answer a person's action, and reduced motion must be respected.
when: Product UI, state changes, page transitions, anything that should ship with no JS library.
prompt: Use the frontend-design skill. Add a single orchestrated page-load sequence to the hero and a View Transition between list and detail views. Respect reduced motion.
steps: Agent picks the one moment worth animating.
Writes @keyframes / element.animate() with transform and opacity only.
Wraps it in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference).
Screenshots and critiques the result before shipping.
hook_cmd: grep -q "prefers-reduced-motion" "$f" || echo "⚠️ add a prefers-reduced-motion guard" >&2

outputs.caption: One orchestrated page-load moment in pure CSS; reduced motion falls back to a 200ms fade

name: Algorithmic Art
summary: Anthropic's skill for generative art: the agent writes an algorithmic philosophy, then expresses it as a seeded p5.js sketch with flow fields, particles and noise, plus parameter controls.
when: Generative backgrounds, art pieces, seeded variations you can reproduce.
prompt: Use the algorithmic-art skill. Create a flow-field piece inspired by wind over water, seeded, with sliders for particle count and noise scale.
steps: Agent writes a short algorithmic philosophy (.md).
Implements it as a p5.js sketch with randomSeed/noiseSeed.
Adds UI controls for parameters.
Returns a self-contained HTML artifact.
hook_cmd: grep -q "randomSeed" "$f" || echo "⚠️ sketch is not seeded" >&2

outputs.caption: “Tidal Memory”: seeded p5.js flow field built from the skill's viewer.html template, with philosophy.md

name: Slack GIF Creator
summary: Builds animated GIFs frame by frame with easing helpers and validates them against Slack's size, dimension and frame-count limits for emoji and message GIFs.
when: Custom reaction emoji, celebratory GIFs, tiny looping animations for chat.
prompt: Use the slack-gif-creator skill. Make a 128x128 emoji GIF of a rocket that wobbles and launches, under Slack's emoji size limit.
steps: Agent draws frames with Pillow using easing functions.
Assembles them into a GIF with loop and duration settings.
Runs the skill's validator for Slack constraints.
Outputs a .gif artifact.
code:
frames = [draw_rocket(y=ease_out(t/30) * -80) for t in range(30)]
frames[0].save('rocket.gif', save_all=True,
               append_images=frames[1:], duration=33, loop=0)

outputs.caption: 128×128 rocket emoji, 25 KB, passes the skill's validate_gif() Slack check

name: Animated Video (design kit)
summary: A design-led workflow for short animated videos: storyboard first, then scenes, motion, and an export step.
when: Promo loops and feature announcements where the storyboard matters more than code.
prompt: Use the animated-video skill. Storyboard a 15s feature announcement in 4 scenes, then build and export it.
steps: Agent writes a storyboard with scene durations.
Builds each scene with consistent type and color tokens.
Adds transitions between scenes.
Exports the video artifact.
code:
scenes:
  - hook: 2s   # big claim, kinetic type
  - problem: 4s
  - product: 6s # UI zoom
  - cta: 3s

outputs.caption: Path B: 4-scene storyboard (hook → problem → product → CTA) with TransitionSeries, 10.5s

run: cd remotion-video && npx remotion render Storyboard out/storyboard.mp4

name: Figma Motion (MCP)
output: Motion specs and exported video from Figma
install: Connect the Figma connector in Claude, then load /figma-design-to-code
summary: Reads motion and prototype transitions out of a Figma file so the agent can reproduce them in code, and can export frames as video.
when: Designers animate in Figma and engineers need matching CSS/GSAP timings.
prompt: Read the motion context for this Figma frame and reproduce the transition in CSS with the same durations and easing.
steps: Agent creates a Figma session for the file.
Calls get_motion_context on the frame.
Maps easing/duration to CSS or GSAP.
Returns code plus an optional exported video.
code:
// from get_motion_context: { duration: 300, easing: 'ease-out', type: 'smart-animate' }
.panel { transition: transform 300ms ease-out; }
note: Needs a Figma file to read motion from; no Figma file was provided, so this one has no output yet.
